headline: High-risk shared-MCP and shared-workspace pair: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while MinerU can ingest document content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP server and processes untrusted document content; Roo Code also uses MCP and can read/write workspace files. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if MinerU outputs are fed into Roo Code through shared files or MCP, though no direct default bridge is documented.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into Roo Code prompts or MCP inputs
IF both agents share an MCP server or shared workspace without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable MCP on one side for the session
Route MinerU output through a human review step before Roo Code sees it
Use separate workspaces/directories for the two agents
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from extracted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content-type validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and JSON, while Roo Code can read workspace files and send context to configured model APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from MinerU into Roo Code and then to a third-party backend. The profiles do not show a built-in isolation boundary.
conditions: IF MinerU writes extracted text into a workspace that Roo Code can read
IF Roo Code is configured to send that workspace context to an external model API
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate directory not mounted in Roo Code
Turn off automatic file/context ingestion in Roo Code
Redact secrets from extracted documents before sharing
Use local-only model endpoints for Roo Code during the run
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs or one-way export paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities, while MinerU can use MCP and concurrent inference. If both operate on the same workspace, Roo Code can overwrite or race with MinerU outputs and git state; the profiles show shared-state via filesystem for Roo Code and no locking mechanism.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF MinerU emits files that Roo Code edits or commits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Avoid git operations until outputs are finalized
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing extractor that can produce facts, tables, and OCR text; Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell, git, and browser tools. If Roo Code treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into code changes, commits, or browser actions. No verification step is documented between them.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses MinerU output as source-of-truth without independent verification
IF extracted text contains hallucinated or malformed facts
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on extracted content
Cross-check key facts against the original document
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis until validation passes
Log source-to-action traceability for each claim
requires-engineering: add automated verification against original files

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is positioned as private/offline, while Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress. If regulated documents processed by MinerU are forwarded into Roo Code, residency or retention obligations can be violated by external API transmission. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls or a DPA boundary.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data from MinerU is sent into Roo Code prompts
IF Roo Code uses a non-compliant external model endpoint or retains logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code prompts
Use a compliant/local model endpoint
Disable or minimize logging and retention
Separate jurisdictions/workspaces for sensitive documents
requires-engineering: document a DPA and retention policy boundary
